LESSON: SIGN READING 13.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: VISUALISING AND SUMMARISING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Sign Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to make a relevant summary of a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

• Individually, learner is guided to search

from print and electronic sources and list

down the sensory words and expressions

used to create mental images in a text.

• In pairs, learners are guided to sign read or

read a passage on an interesting issue like

sea travel and pick out the sensory words or

expressions and the mental images they

create in a reader.

• In groups, learners are guided to fill in

templates requiring key ideas from the text

or parts of the text and display the

templates on the wall,

• In groups, learners are guided to sign read

or read a text on current issues such as

responsible sea travel and identify the main

ideas in a paragraph or a passage.

• Individually, learner is guided to

summarise the ideas in own words in charts

and share for peer review.
